title: Scripture rather shows it hidden: Isaiah 55:8-9 and Romans 11:33-34
source_text: L. Imo satis indicat rem esse quam Deus voluit humanis ingeniis esse occultam atque imperviam, & in cujus profundum mentis nostrae acies penetrare non valet. Quo pertinet illud Dei apud Isaiam. Non enim cogitationes meae, cogitationes vestrae; neque viae vestrae viae meae. Quia sicut exaltantur coeli a terra, sic exaltatae sunt viae meae a viis vestris, & cogitationes meae a cogitationibus vestris: Item illud Apostoli in epistola ad Romanos, O Altitudo divitiarum sapientiae & scientiae Dei: quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus, & investigabiles viae ejus! Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini? Aut quis consiliarius ejus fuit?
pass_a_gloss: L. Nay it sufficiently indicates that it is a matter which God willed to be hidden and impassable to human wits, and into whose depth the edge of our mind cannot penetrate. To which pertains that word of God in Isaiah. For my thoughts are not your thoughts; nor your ways my ways. Because as the heavens are exalted from the earth, so are my ways exalted from your ways, and my thoughts from your thoughts: Likewise that of the Apostle in the epistle to the Romans, O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God: how incomprehensible are his judgements, and unsearchable his ways! For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who was his counsellor?
pass_b_english: Indeed, it shows clearly enough that this is something God willed to be hidden from human minds and closed to them, a depth our mind's sharpest sight cannot reach.

This is what God says in Isaiah: 'For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so are my ways high above your ways and my thoughts above your thoughts.'

So too the Apostle in the letter to the Romans: 'O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgements, and unsearchable his ways! For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counsellor?'
